questions.prompt: A force of 25 N pushes a box 6 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
A student lifts a 3 kg bag (weight 29.4 N) up 2 m onto a shelf. How much work is done on the bag?
In which case is NO work done on the object?
options: A guard holds a heavy bag without moving
A horse pulls a cart along a road
A girl pushes a cycle forward
questions.explain: No displacement means no work, however hard it feels.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of work?
questions.explain: Work = force × distance: N × m = J.

feedback.1: The watt is the unit of power (joules per second).

questions.prompt: A porter carries a suitcase along a flat platform. How much work does his upward holding force do on the suitcase?
options: Zero, because the force is at right angles to the motion
Equal to the weight × distance walked
Negative, because the suitcase is heavy
questions.explain: His force is upward; the motion is horizontal. A force at right angles to the motion does no work.

questions.prompt: Friction acts on a box as it slides to a stop. What kind of work does friction do?
options: It depends on the colour of the floor
No work: friction never does work
Negative work: it takes energy away from the box
Positive work: it gives the box energy
questions.explain: Friction acts against the motion, so it removes kinetic energy (turning it into heat).

questions.prompt: A force does 480 J of work pushing a trolley 12 m. What is the size of the force?
Explain why a person pushing hard against a wall that doesn’t move feels tired but does no work on the wall.
questions.modelAnswer: Work is done only when a force moves an object in the direction of the force. The wall does not move, so the displacement is zero and W = F × 0 = 0. The person feels tired because their muscles still use chemical energy (transferred as heat inside the body) to stay tense, but none of it is transferred to the wall.
rubric: The wall does not move, so W = 0
Muscles still use energy, released as heat
questions.explain: Criterion A: using the physics definition of work.
